14. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However he has produced Ex.P.16 Aadhaar card.

Eventhough the said Aadhaar card is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of cogent evidence with respect to date of birth of petitioner, the said document can be relied upon, according to which t
Therefore, it appears that as (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.608/2022 on the date of accident the age of petitioner is 30 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 30 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 years is 17.

With regard to avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2021 to be taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,000/-.
